newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says Focus 2000 well on track.
newsitem.headline: KLM says Focus 2000 well on track.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM said on Wednesday its Focus 2000 programme to boost operating revenues was well on track and would start yielding benefits over the current 1997/98 financial year.
"Important advantages (of Focus 2000) may be expected during the current year and even more in the year thereafter," KLM President Pieter Bouw told a results news conference.
He said the programme, aimed at boosting operating revenues by 1.5 billion guilders over three years, went back to basics: "We're working at (a) pretty fundamental (level)," Bouw said.
Announced last November, Focus 2000 had not had a significant impact on results in the 1996/97 year, he said.
Bouw said KLM had so far instituted 45 of a total 74 projects under the programme.

These included a "segment and branding study" looking into which services and products could profitably be exploited in various market segments and its Hub in Transfer project to cut unit costs by some 30 percent through better process management.

KLM, which earlier reported full-year 1996/97 net profits down at 236 million guilders after a one-off 290 million guilder charge for the Focus 2000 programme, said it saw operating profits improving significantly over the current year.
